metadata.name: Dyslexia Support Skill
metadata.description: Clinical and accommodation framework for dyslexia as a neurodevelopmental cognitive disorder — a lifelong, brain-based difference in phonological and orthographic processing architecture (left temporoparietal cortex, visual word form area, inferior frontal gyrus). Covers the full lifespan: K-12 special education, higher education, workplace, and adult accommodation across three legal jurisdictions. Distinguishes remediation targets (trainable skills) from bypass targets (persistent deficits requiring permanent cognitive prosthetics). Grounded in Shaywitz phonological deficit theory, Dehaene VWFA research, Gabrieli neuroimaging evidence, DSM-5 Specific Learning Disorder (315.00), and ICD-11 Developmental Learning Disorder (6A03.0). Multi-jurisdiction legal framework support: United States (IDEA, Section 504, ADA Title I/II/III), France (Loi n° 2005-102, Code de l'éducation, PAP/PPS via MDPH/CDAPH, RQTH for workplace), and Spain (LOE/LOMLOE, ACNEAE/DEA framework, ACNS pathway, 17-Comunidad Autónoma regional implementations).
metadata.author: Justice

skills.name: standards-compliance
skills.description: Regulatory compliance framework treating dyslexia as a neurodevelopmental cognitive disorder across the full lifespan and three legal jurisdictions. **United States**: clinical frameworks (DSM-5 Specific Learning Disorder 315.00, ICD-11 Developmental Learning Disorder 6A03.0), IDA Knowledge and Practice Standards for Teachers of Reading 2018 (all 5 domains: foundation concepts, reading profiles, assessment, structured literacy teaching, ethics), K-12 special education law (IDEA specific learning disability identification, IEP requirements, FAPE, procedural safeguards), Section 504 (K-12 accommodations, eligibility differences from IDEA, major life activity determinations), higher education (Section 504 at postsecondary institutions, ADA Title II for public colleges, ADA Title III for private colleges, Office for Civil Rights complaint procedures), and workplace (ADA Title I reasonable accommodations, undue hardship analysis, disability disclosure, EEOC procedures). **France**: Loi n° 2005-102 (Loi Handicap), Code de l'éducation Art. L321-4 mandatory accommodations, PAP (Circulaire 2015-016 — K-12 pedagogical accommodation, school physician validation), PPS via MDPH/CDAPH (K-12, when AESH/ULIS/state-funded equipment needed), aménagements d'examens (Circulaire 2023-033 — Brevet/Baccalauréat tiers-temps, secrétaire lecteur/scripteur), bilan orthophonique workflow, post-K-12 transitions (CFA accommodations, RQTH for workplace), FR–US crosswalk. **Spain**: LOE/LOMLOE (Art. 71-72, 79 bis), ACNEAE/DEA framework (DEA — *not* NEE — for dyslexia/dyscalculia), ACNS (Adaptaciones Curriculares No Significativas — primary tool, not ACS), Informe Psicopedagógico requirements, EBAU/EvAU exam accommodations (Arial 16pt, 1.5 line spacing), 17-Comunidad Autónoma regional variation, ES–US crosswalk. Includes neuroscience-informed Cognitive Disorder Accommodation checklist distinguishing trainable skills from persistent deficits requiring permanent cognitive prosthetics.

skills.name: gap-analysis
skills.description: Systematic gap identification across the dyslexia cognitive support ecosystem, spanning education, clinical practice, workplace, and consumer technology — with cross-linguistic / cross-jurisdictional analysis for US/FR/ES. Identifies 12 critical gaps including retroactive vs. proactive accessibility, absence of personalized accommodation engines, passive vs. interactive assistive tools, fragmented tool ecosystems, disconnected progress monitoring, assessment-to-instruction pipeline breakdowns, practitioner implementation support gaps, missing dyslexia-specific UX design standards, workplace accommodation gaps, clinical-educational framing gaps, plus four cross-linguistic gaps: cross-linguistic assessment tool availability (CTOPP-2/WRMT vs. PROLEC-R/BELEC/L2MA-2/Timé3 by language), fluency-first intervention programs for transparent orthographies (Spanish), EdTech locale-awareness (FR/ES default settings, normed readability, phonics sequences), and legal framework crosswalk for internationally mobile families with DYS children. Includes pre-built measures: Dyslexia-Friendly Content Audit Checklist, Dyslexia UX Heuristics (12 heuristics extending Nielsen's 10), Cognitive Prosthetics Maturity Model, and cross-linguistic comparison matrix.

skills.name: remediation-strategies
skills.description: Evidence-based intervention and cognitive prosthetics framework for dyslexia grounded in structured literacy and Orton-Gillingham methodology, with locale-specific orthographic adaptations. Explicitly distinguishes two target types: (1) **Remediation targets** — trainable skills that improve with instruction (phonological awareness, decoding accuracy, fluency, spelling patterns, morphological knowledge), addressed through structured literacy's six elements (phonology, sound-symbol association, syllable instruction, morphology, syntax, semantics) following OG principles (multisensory, explicit, diagnostic/prescriptive, sequential/cumulative, individualized), implemented via evidence-based programs (Wilson Reading System, Barton, Lindamood-Bell LiPS, Sonday, RAVE-O, Alphabetic Phonics for English; Méthode Borel-Maisonny, Chassymo, ERCOLE, ITECO for French; PRODISLEX, LECTOESCRIPTURA programs for Spanish); and (2) **Bypass targets** — persistent cognitive processing differences requiring permanent cognitive prosthetics (text-to-speech for reading load, speech-to-text for writing, spell/grammar checkers, audiobook access via Learning Ally/Bookshare/Vocale Presse for FR/Audible.es for Spanish, OCR for scanned materials, reading rulers, dyslexia-friendly fonts, real-time captioning, extended time as neurological accommodation). Locale-aware orthographic context: English (opaque — accuracy-dominant), French (semi-opaque — accuracy + spelling-morphology), Spanish (transparent — fluency-dominant). Includes lifespan application from K-12 tutoring through adult workplace AT stacks, with French orthophoniste delivery system and Spanish ACNS-driven school remediation discussion.

skills.name: document-generation
skills.description: Professional document templates for the full lifespan of dyslexia accommodation needs across three jurisdictions. **K-12 educational (US)**: IEPs, Section 504 Accommodation Plans, Progress Monitoring Reports, Prior Written Notice (PWN), RTI/Intervention Documentation. **K-12 educational (France)**: PAP standardized template per Circulaire 2015-016 (four cycle versions: maternelle/élémentaire/collège/lycée), MDPH dossier support package for PPS request (Cerfa 15692*01 + 15695*01 + bilans), demande d'aménagements d'examens (Brevet/Baccalauréat per Circulaire 2023-033). **K-12 educational (Spain)**: Informe Psicopedagógico template, ACNS (Adaptaciones Curriculares No Significativas) documentation, EBAU/EvAU exam accommodation request. **Higher education**: Section 504/ADA disability services request letters, accommodation letters to faculty, testing accommodation requests; FR university aménagements via service handicap; ES universidad ACNEAE adaptation requests. **Workplace**: ADA Title I reasonable accommodation request letters (US), RQTH application support (FR — Reconnaissance de la Qualité de Travailleur Handicapé via MDPH), Spain workplace accommodation requests (Ley General de Discapacidad 1/2013), interactive process documentation. **Clinical**: Psychoeducational evaluation summaries (US: CTOPP-2, WRMT-III, GORT-5, KTEA-3, WISC-V, Nelson-Denny; FR: bilan orthophonique, BMT-i, WISC-V French norms; ES: PROLEC-R, BELEC adaptations, WISC-V Spanish norms), DSM-5/ICD-11 diagnostic summary letters, cognitive prosthetics prescription letters. **General**: Dyslexia screening checklists (early childhood, school-age, adult — locale-appropriate), parent/self-advocacy communication letters in EN/FR/ES.

commands.name: dyslexia-audit
commands.description: Audit a program, tool, curriculum, workplace policy, or content for compliance with dyslexia cognitive accommodation requirements across three jurisdictions. **United States** (locale=us, default): evaluates against IDA Knowledge and Practice Standards, structured literacy fidelity, IDEA/504 for K-12, Section 504/ADA for higher education, ADA Title I for workplace, ADA Title III for public accommodations. **France** (locale=fr): evaluates against Loi 2005-102 / Code de l'éducation Art. L321-4, PAP compliance per Circulaire 2015-016, PPS/MDPH process compliance, exam aménagements consistency per Circulaire 2023-033, qualified-professional assessment (bilan orthophonique, neuropsychologique). **Spain** (locale=es): evaluates against LOE/LOMLOE, correct ACNEAE classification (DEA — not NEE — for dyslexia/dyscalculia), ACNS documentation requirements, Informe Psicopedagógico completeness, EBAU/EvAU accommodation consistency, regional Comunidad Autónoma legislation when --region specified. Generates comprehensive audit report with findings, composite score (A-F grade), and remediation roadmap covering structured literacy coverage, cognitive prosthetics availability, accommodation adequacy, and UDL principles. FR/ES audits include US crosswalk references. Creates audit files in audits/ subdirectory.

project_name.description: Name of the project, material, program, workplace policy, or tool being audited

context.description: Regulatory and population context for audit

locale.description: Legal-framework locale: 'us' (IDEA/504/IDA/ADA), 'fr' (France: Loi 2005-102, PAP/PPS, RQTH for workplace), or 'es' (Spain: LOE/LOMLOE, ACNEAE/DEA, ACNS)

region.description: For locale=es: Comunidad Autónoma (e.g. 'madrid', 'cataluna', 'andalucia', 'pais-vasco', 'valencia', 'galicia') to apply region-specific legislation. Ignored for locale=us and locale=fr.

commands.name: generate-iep
commands.displayName: Generate Accommodation Document (IEP, 504, ADA, Workplace, PAP, ACNS)
commands.description: Generate a comprehensive, legally-compliant accommodation document tailored to the individual's context and jurisdiction. **United States**: (1) IEP — K-12 special education with PLAAFP, SMART goals for phonological awareness/decoding/fluency/comprehension/writing, structured literacy-aligned services, cognitive prosthetics accommodations, LRE documentation; (2) 504 Plan — K-12 or higher education accommodations; (3) Workplace Accommodation Request — ADA Title I reasonable accommodation letter to employer/HR with documentation of functional impact, specific requested accommodations, and interactive process invitation; (4) Higher Ed Disability Services Request — university disability office documentation. **France**: PAP (Plan d'Accompagnement Personnalisé per Circulaire 2015-016 — four cycle templates), MDPH dossier support package for PPS request (Cerfa forms + bilans), demande d'aménagements d'examens (Brevet/Baccalauréat per Circulaire 2023-033), RQTH application support for adults entering workplace. **Spain**: Informe Psicopedagógico, ACNS documentation, EBAU/EvAU exam accommodation request, ACNEAE classification documentation. **Cross-jurisdiction**: clinical summary letters citing DSM-5/ICD-11 diagnoses. Includes comorbidity considerations (ADHD, dyscalculia, anxiety, APD, executive function).

person_name.description: Individual's full name (student, employee, or self-advocate)

grade_or_role.description: Current grade level, program/major, or job title

document_type.description: Type of document to generate. US: iep, 504, ada-workplace-request, higher-ed-dsr, clinical-summary. France: pap, pps-dossier, fr-exam-accommodation, rqth-application. Spain: informe-psicopedagogico, acns, es-exam-accommodation.

locale.description: Jurisdiction. Selects native-language document vocabulary and legal references. Must be consistent with document_type (e.g. document_type=pap requires locale=fr).

region.description: For locale=es: Comunidad Autónoma for region-specific document variants (e.g. Cataluña uses NESE terminology in some documents).

fr_cycle.description: For locale=fr K-12 documents: school cycle. PAP template version varies by cycle.

cognitive_prosthetics.description: Cognitive prosthetics to include in accommodations

commands.name: remediation-plan
commands.description: Create a comprehensive support plan with TWO parallel tracks, with locale-aware program selection: (1) **Remediation track** — structured literacy instruction addressing trainable skills via the six elements (phonology, sound-symbol association, syllable instruction, morphology, syntax, semantics) and OG principles (multisensory, explicit, diagnostic/prescriptive, sequential/cumulative, individualized), implemented through evidence-based programs (US: Wilson, Barton, LiPS, Sonday, RAVE-O, Alphabetic Phonics; FR: Méthode Borel-Maisonny, Chassymo, ERCOLE, ITECO — typically delivered by orthophoniste with prescription; ES: PRODISLEX, LECTOESCRIPTURA, fluency-first programs reflecting Spanish transparent orthography); (2) **Cognitive prosthetics track** — permanent assistive technology stack addressing persistent processing differences (text-to-speech, speech-to-text, audiobook access via Learning Ally/Bookshare/Vocale Presse FR/Audible ES, OCR tools, spell/grammar checkers in target language, dyslexia-friendly fonts, reading rulers). Includes lesson templates for remediation track, AT setup and training for prosthetics track, progress monitoring for both, and lifespan adaptations (K-12 through adult/workplace). Locale-aware orthographic context: English (opaque — accuracy-dominant), French (semi-opaque — morphological-spelling-heavy), Spanish (transparent — fluency-dominant).

locale.description: Locale: drives program-pool selection (US: Wilson/Barton/LiPS; FR: Borel-Maisonny/Chassymo/ITECO; ES: PRODISLEX/fluency-focused) and orthographic-context defaults

current_level.description: Current reading level and profile description

intervention_duration.description: Intervention duration (use 'ongoing' for adult cognitive prosthetics plans)

intensity.description: Intensity level (Tier 1/2/3 for K-12, session frequency for adult). Note: French orthophonie default 1-2x/week is often insufficient for moderate-severe — flag intensity gap explicitly when locale=fr.

focus_areas.description: Focus areas. 'morphology' especially relevant for FR (semi-opaque). 'fluency' especially relevant for ES (transparent). 'cognitive-prosthetics-only' for adults where remediation is not the primary goal.

program.description: Evidence-based program. US: wilson, barton, lindamood-bell, sonday, rave-o, alphabetic-phonics, ortongillingham-general, adult-literacy-focused. France: borel-maisonny, chassymo, ercole, iteco. Spain: prodislex, lectoescritura.

prosthetics_stack.description: Assistive technology stack: TTS tools, STT tools, audiobook services, OCR, etc.

anxiety_considerations.description: Include reading or disclosure anxiety management strategies

commands.name: content-accessibility-check
commands.description: Audit educational, workplace, or consumer content for dyslexia-friendly design across 10 dimensions: typography (font family, size, spacing, weight — dyslexic-friendly fonts like Lexend, Atkinson Hyperlegible, OpenDyslexic), readability (Flesch-Kincaid level for English, Flesch-Szigriszt or Crawford for Spanish, Kandel/Moles for French; sentence length, cognitive load), color and contrast (WCAG compliance, off-white backgrounds, low-contrast pairs), layout (whitespace, line length 45-65 characters, left-alignment), cognitive load (chunking, scaffolding, working memory demands), navigation predictability, assistive technology compatibility (screen reader semantic HTML, text-to-speech parseability, proper heading hierarchy), multimedia accessibility (captions, transcripts, audio descriptions), UDL principles application, and cognitive accommodation integration. **Locale-aware checks**: FR — diacritics rendering (é, è, ê, ë, à, â, ç, î, ï, ô, œ, ù, û, ü, ÿ) at body size, ligatures (œ), French dyslexia accommodation norms (Arial/OpenDyslexic ≥14pt per Circulaire 2015-016), prohibited full justification per PAP guidance; ES — tilde/accent rendering (á, é, í, ó, ú, ü, ñ, ¿, ¡), fluency-supportive design priority (Spanish is transparent — fluency deficit dominates), EBAU/EvAU exam content checked against Arial 16pt + 1.5 line spacing standard, flag automated spelling-penalty grading systems. Applies to K-12 textbooks, higher-ed courseware, workplace training, consumer apps, and government/healthcare communications.

content_name.description: Name or description of the content being checked

locale.description: Locale for typography, diacritics, readability-formula, and orthographic checks. 'fr' applies French diacritic + ligature rendering checks and PAP/Circulaire 2015-016 standards. 'es' applies Spanish tilde rendering and EBAU/EvAU standards (Arial 16pt + 1.5 line spacing).

templates.name: audit-report-template
templates.description: Standard template for dyslexia cognitive accommodation audit reports covering IDA standards, structured literacy compliance, WCAG 2.1 AA, ADA where applicable, and dyslexia-specific UX heuristics. Locale variants: includes FR-US and ES-US crosswalk sections when audit is conducted with locale=fr or locale=es.
